sections.overview: This Asian hairstreak belongs to the lycaenid tribe Cheritrini, also collectively called “imperials” in English.
sections.identification: Indian records distinguish the regional subspecies Cheritra freja butleri and Cheritra freja evansi.
sections.habitat: A field survey recorded it at forest edges around Matheran in western India.
sections.diet: Its Indian caterpillars use host plants from Fabaceae, Lauraceae, Rubiaceae and Sapindaceae.
sections.behavior: At Matheran, adults were seen mud-puddling, basking, and visiting sap, carcasses, dung, bird droppings and rotting fruit.
sections.reproduction: The sources document larval host plants but provide little species-specific detail on courtship, egg laying or brood timing.
sections.ecology: Its larvae use plants from several families, while adults also exploit mineral-rich soil and diverse organic matter.
sections.conservation: The reviewed sources document Indian distribution and natural history but provide no current global conservation assessment.
